latest_release.name: v12.6.0
latest_release.body:
## v12.6.0 (2026-11-20)

#### Notable changes

**New features**
* `NestFactory.create()` infers the application type from the adapter: `NestFactory.create(AppModule, new FastifyAdapter())` returns a `NestFastifyApplication` with no type argument, and the same goes for `ExpressAdapter` and `NodeAdapter`. An explicit type argument still works. A custom adapter declares its application type as the fourth type argument of `AbstractHttpAdapter` – [#18623](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18623)
* `WsAdapter` takes `gracefulShutdown` (`false` by default) and `gracePeriod` (10,000 ms by default). With `gracefulShutdown`, closing the application stops accepting connections (an upgrade on a server shared with the HTTP adapter gets a 503), ignores new messages, waits up to `gracePeriod` for message handlers and pending replies, and closes each socket with code 1001 – [#18589](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18589)
* gRPC server: `gracePeriod` (10,000 ms by default) for `gracefulShutdown` – [#18566](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18566)

**New defaults and behaviour changes**
* gRPC server with `gracefulShutdown`: closing used to wait for the calls in progress with no limit; calls still running after `gracePeriod` are now cancelled. Raise `gracePeriod` for long-running streams – [#18566](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18566)
* A custom parameter decorator that gives the handler the response object now passes it as it is, and no pipe runs on it, as with `@Res()`, whatever the adapter. On Fastify such a handler used to never run – [#18600](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18600)
* A method that overrides a `@Res({ passthrough: true })` handler with a plain `@Res()` no longer inherits `passthrough` – [#18617](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18617)
* `DiscoveryService` finds a class that extends a class decorated with a `DiscoveryService.createDecorator()` decorator under that decorator – [#18582](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18582)
* Route conflict detection reads string hosts as patterns, so a route on `:tenant.example.com` is found to overlap one on `admin.example.com`, and such routes may now be reported – [#18609](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18609)
* The `createNestApplication()` and `createNestMicroservice()` of a testing module apply `logger` and `forceConsole` as `NestFactory` does: `logger: true` keeps the logger (it used to turn logging off), and `forceConsole: true` logs through `console` – [#18618](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18618)
* `@nestjs/platform-node`: a `Content-Type` set with `res.setHeader()` gets `charset=utf-8` when `res.send()` sends a string, as on Express – [#18527](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18527)
* `@nestjs/platform-fastify`: the exception for a failed upload carries the parser's error as its `cause`, as on Express – [#18555](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18555)
* `@nestjs/platform-fastify`: the router answers a request whose target does not start with `/` (other than `*` and absolute-form URLs) with a 400 (`FST_ERR_BAD_URL`), after `find-my-way` 9.10.2; such a request used to reach the not-found handler – [#18569](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18569)
* `inject()` on `@nestjs/platform-fastify` and `@nestjs/platform-node`: a response to `HEAD`, and a 204 or 304 response, has no body, after `light-my-request` 6.8.1 – [#18570](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18570)

**Microservices**
* NATS and MQTT servers closed before their client connects: `listen()` fails with "Connection closed" instead of starting – [#18602](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18602), [#18603](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18603)
* Clients fail pending requests with "Connection closed" where they used to leave them waiting: Kafka when the reply consumer stops or crashes, or a rebalance moves its reply partition away – [#18583](https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/18583); MQTT and Redis when closed before the reply subscription is confirmed – [#18584](https://github.
